- [FACT] User's family has a wide age range, from young children to elderly grandparents.
- [FACT] User will be using rectangular tables for the gathering.
- [FACT] The gathering will take place at the user's parents' house.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested using a mix of table sizes for different group sizes and conversations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended a "hub-and-spoke" layout for the tables.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested setting up a separate kids' table or area for younger children.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a rough outline for seating arrangements, including 2-3 larger tables for adults and older children and 2-3 smaller tables for younger children or smaller family groups.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant emphasized leaving space between tables for comfortable movement and designated areas for buffet lines or activities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested a seating arrangement prioritizing ease of movement and accessibility for elderly family members.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended a U-shape or gentle curve for the main table layout.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant advised placing elderly family members at the ends of the tables for easier access.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested leaving 3-4 feet of clearance between tables for wheelchair accessibility.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended a few extra chairs or tables for last-minute adjustments.
- [USER] User expressed satisfaction with the seating arrangement plan.
